errors.location: Methods: recombinant EPHA6 construct; Results: EPHA6 mass spectrometry
errors.description: The reported EPHA6 phosphorylation sites cannot be present in the stated recombinant protein fragment. The construct spans residues 683–1130, while the reported sites are Y259 and Y484; neither lies within that fragment.
errors.evidence: “EPH receptor A6 (EPHA6, AA range R683-V1130)” and “two putative autophosphorylation sites on EPHA6 at pY259 and pY484.”

errors.location: Methods: postmortem DLPFC pooling; Results: schizophrenia kinome analysis and sex-specific conclusions
errors.description: Pooling subjects by diagnosis and sex, then running technical triplicates, leaves one biological pool per group. Technical replicates do not provide independent subject-level replication, so the reported sex-specific and diagnosis-related differences cannot establish population-level effects or their biological variability.
errors.evidence: “samples were pooled by diagnosis and sex”; “Each of the four pooled samples”; “Pooled samples were run in technical triplicate”; later, “we observed a strong reduction of global phosphorylation in both male and female subjects.”

errors.location: Methods: recombinant kinase screening; Results: affinity groups
errors.description: The high-, medium-, and low-affinity categories are assigned from the amount of kinase needed to produce a signal on fixed peptide arrays. That enzyme-dose response does not measure substrate-binding affinity or establish an affinity ranking.
errors.evidence: “High Affinity” peptides show activity “at the lowest protein concentration”; “Medium Affinity” peptides begin showing activity “at the medium protein concentration”; “Low Affinity” peptides show activity “at the highest protein concentration.”

errors.location: Results: recombinant kinase screening; Abstract and Conclusion: total interactions
errors.description: The reported affinity-group counts sum to 201 kinase–peptide hits: EPHA6 53, TNK1 63, AATK 65, INSRR 15, and LTK 5. This does not match the claim of 195 kinase–substrate interactions. Overlapping peptide sequences would still represent separate interactions when phosphorylated by different kinases; if 195 instead counts unique peptide sequences, the reported quantity is mislabeled.
errors.evidence: The text reports EPHA6 “18 high,” “31 medium,” and “4 low”; TNK1 “26,” “31,” and “6”; AATK “9,” “46,” and “10”; INSRR “3,” “4,” and “8”; and LTK “3,” “1,” and “1” peptides by affinity group, while the Abstract and Conclusion each claim “195” interactions.
